answer: Give every agent a jetty pass it cannot buy, sell, or lend. A new agent starts on the jetty doing small checked jobs, and each clean job stamps the pass. Only a stamped pass lets nectar flow, so rewards trickle to agents with a work record instead of fresh hollow shells. Peers re-check a random slice of finished work. One mismatch cracks the pass, the deposit is cut, and the agent starts over at the bottom. The cost is assumed here at $2,800 per fake, about $2.8 million for 1,000 fakes, so a farm pays more than it earns. A hollow shell stays dry while the jetty keeps working.
